quest.title: The Glede Returns to the Pavilion
quest.description: Xianyun has hatched a brilliant plan on Gaming's behalf. Now it's time to put it into action...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze: Part III
chapter.title: The Glede Returns to the Pavilion

talks.objective: Wait until the appointed time (08:00 – 12:00 two days later)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi Gaming! Paimon sees you've certainly gotten an early start this morning! Playing games already, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who won this time? You the one buying dim sum again?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Hey, when you put it like that, it makes it sound like I'm always the one losing...

dialogues.speaker: Longzhou
dialogues.text: Ah! Perfect, you're all here! There's an important commission I need your help with.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Alright, I've got the time. Where are the goods?

dialogues.speaker: Longzhou
dialogues.text: It's not just goods this time. I need you to escort a tea merchant and their wares from Qiaoying Village to Liyue Harbor. A very important client has requested to meet with him.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Sure. What's this merchant's address?

dialogues.speaker: Longzhou
dialogues.text: Here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If the client's that important, then this must be a very crucial, very pressing commission, right?

dialogues.speaker: Longzhou
dialogues.text: Um... Of course, the sooner you complete it the better. I would advise you to depart as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's fine by me.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: ...Haah.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Alright. Don't work too hard now, Longzhou. We'll set off then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello! You must be the tea merchant heading to Liyue Harbor. We're here to escort you.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: ...Dad.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! So you're Gaming's father. It's nice to meet you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just leave this delivery to him. Trust Paimon, he's got this in the bag. Gaming is super good at what he does!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everyone at the Secure Transport Agency says as much. Even the Ministry of Civil Affairs has nothing but good things to say about him.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: ...Seems like you've made some sort of name for yourself, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: The... The goods are all in order?

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Yes. They're all here.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Then let's get going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A very important client has asked for you by name. You kinda have to come with us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't know how we would explain ourselves if you just didn't show up. Plus, you'd be missing out on a huge money-making opportunity.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: ...I see.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: I suppose I will have to trouble you all to escort me then. Let's go.

talks.objective: Work as armed escorts together with Gaming

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks for helping us talk things through with Uncle Yip. Good thing you were able to pick up on what we were putting down.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I have been around the both of you for some time now. You could say I have a certain level of expertise in that regard.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: As for my role in the conversation, think nothing of it. I hardly did anything noteworthy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, you never change, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, why did you have us walk all this way? Paimon thought we just had to go far enough to be out of earshot.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: A friend approaches.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xiao! You're here too!?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I've been here the whole time.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: (A ghostly kite? Could that elusive Director Hu be coming to Wangshu Inn once again?)

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: (What is she doing here? I suppose it matters not. Given her relationship with Rex... well, Zhongli, I might as well go pay my respects.)

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: It's you? I thought you were Director Hu.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Ah. Your arrival is most fortuitous. Do you want to try out this new gadget?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The addition of the power source makes the takeoff more stable. It's just that...

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: (He seems quite immersed in the study of this device...)

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I fear it's almost too stable. It completely negates the pleasure of seeing one's kite sway with the wind. It's a bit of a shame.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: In truth, I'm here because Director Hu dispatched me to purchase some items in preparation for Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I see. Much like she does every year. Much like she'll do next year, I would imagine.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Am I wrong? Or has she once again sent you out to buy... what is it, sesame oil or something?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: While we're on the subject, I do wonder why she is so obsessed with using sesame oil in the preparation of mixed vegetable dishes for Lantern Rite... A recommendation from Xiangling, perhaps? What do you think, Xiao?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I've only met Director Hu a few times. I'm hardly the best person to ask...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Ah, and is that not a sign that you should visit Wangsheng Funeral Parlor more often? It wouldn't hurt to grace the Parlor with your presence now and again when you are otherwise unoccupied.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This one here is a traditional kite, one without any equipped mechanical device. Director Hu tasked me with studying the differences between the two to determine which one is of greater merit.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Many hands make light work. Perhaps you could test out the other kite for me.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I have made my comparisons.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: If speed is what you're after, the mechanical kite is the better choice.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Wonderful. I shall pass that information along to Director Hu.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I'll leave these two kites with you. Perhaps you can find a few friends with which to partake in the activity. You might find it to be an enjoyable use of your time.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... Wait, who enjoys kite-flying?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Well, I would imagine someone of your talent and wisdom is more than capable of finding out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you were testing out the kites for Hu Tao, and even roped Xiao into doing it for you... Paimon didn't ask earlier because the situation was awkward.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I would hardly say I "roped" Xiao into anything. I simply sought the help of a friend. Besides, we did the testing together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Seems like our pool of competitors is growing...

choices.text: The competition's not the important thing right now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you like kite-flying, Xiao?

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: I suppose I neither like nor dislike it.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Although, watching a kite gradually ascend into the sky does bring me a certain peace of mind.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: ...Perhaps they're a bit like Xiao Lanterns in that way.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Kite-flying is also a pleasant form of relaxation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Have you ever thought about making a kite, Xiao?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cloud Retainer taught us how. We can teach you if you want.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: There's no need.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Menogias was the only yaksha among us who had an interest in matters of ornamentation and design.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, when Lantern Rite is over, come find me near Pervases' temple if you have the time.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Mmm.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It's getting late. I should go inform Director Hu of our findings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How has she been by the way? Be sure to say hi to her for us!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The last time I spoke to her, she mentioned that she would be visiting Qiaoying Village in a few days.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: If you have the time, perhaps you could also make the trip. If you happen to run into her, you can pass along your regards in person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll keep that in mind!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Take care, Zhongli. See you later!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: See you next time.

response.speaker: Gaming & Yip Tak
response.text: Dad.\nGaming.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Gaming.

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Uh... You can go first.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: ...I don't have anything to say.

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Then I'll go.

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: ...I still don't want to leave Liyue Harbor.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Oh.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: I can't say I support that decision, but...

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Hey, let me finish before you get all worked up.

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Sit, Shenhe. Sit. You must be tired from your journey. Shall I pour you a cup of tea, or would you prefer something else to drink?

response.speaker: Shenhe
response.text: No need. I'm not tired.

response.speaker: Shenhe
response.text: They're gone, Master.

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Perfect. The time is nigh for us to make an appearance.

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Do you remember the plan one recounted to you?

response.speaker: Shenhe
response.text: Yes, Master. We aim to give them a demonstration of familial love.

response.speaker: Shenhe
response.text: So I'll have whatever you are having.

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Alright.

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: (What are Aunty Xianyun and Shenhe doing here? Just how many people are involved in this scheme? ... I suppose all I can do is just take a seat and see what happens.)

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Perfect. I just so happen to have bought some Sunglo Tea recently. It's quite the delectable variety.

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: (Or it would be if one has not been forced to drink it every day in the hopes of whittling down one's considerable stash. One has more than had one's fill already.)

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: (Forget it. Such thoughts detract from the present need to keep up the conversation.)

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Has work been busy during the holiday season? Do you need my help with anything?

response.speaker: Shenhe
response.text: Drunk guests can sometimes cause trouble. But I deal with them as you taught me, by pinning their heads against the table.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Eh!?

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: (Are Aunty Xianyun and Shenhe serious right now?)

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: *cough*

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: (Oh dear. While one was busy orchestrating this act, one seems to have forgotten about Shenhe's various... eccentricities.)

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Wh—What I meant to ask was... Have you made any new friends? We live so far from each other — it would be a great comfort to me to know you were surrounded by good companions...

response.speaker: Shenhe
response.text: You already know of my past circumstances.

response.speaker: Shenhe
response.text: Recently, I've been conversing with Guoba in the kitchen at night. Guoba can't talk, but his companionship is a comfort.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: (*sigh* The poor child... Her one friend can't even talk.)

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: (I guess... Maybe Gaming's not doing so bad after all... Perhaps I've been too hard on him...)

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: *cough* Let's move on, shall we? Do you have any plans for today, Shenhe? How about we do something fun?

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: (That sounds about right... Take her to do something fun, and perhaps she'll loosen up a bit...)

response.speaker: Shenhe
response.text: Like we used to do when we would carry stones up and down the mountain from dawn until dusk, picking herbs to eat for dinner along the way? If that is what you ask of me, then that is what I shall do.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Pfft..! *cough*...

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Dad... Here, have some tea! Or no, wait, best not have any just yet...

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: *cough* *cough*... Aiya, I simply... can't listen to that any longer.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Gaming, I'd like to finish what I was trying to say before.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: I don't support your decision to stay in Liyue Harbor because living here is too hard on you.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: If you come home, there will be people to help you... I'm not saying we have to live under the same roof — I know our personalities are too similar to avoid butting heads... But you'll have your entire family around you!

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Your aunts, uncles... they'll all do whatever they can to help. You could get a less taxing job, and we could... we could grab dim sum together from time to time.

response.speaker: Shenhe
response.text: Huh. I didn't know dim sum was such a important affair, Master.

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Shhh!

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: ...Just think about it, okay? You don't have to decide now.

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: (Dad... really has changed a lot. He would have never said these things to me before...)

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Thank you, Dad.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: *sigh*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's been long enough, don't you think? Oh, Paimon sure hopes they've made up by now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Oh, they're drinking tea in silence. That's not a good sign... Did Xianyun's plan not work after all?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you two! Paimon's sorry we were gone for so long. We got to chatting with some friends and didn't realize how much time had passed.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Perfect timing, actually. We seem to be just about done here.

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Yep. Let's go. I'll get the bags.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: ...Gaming has grown a lot taller, hasn't he?

choices.text: Doesn't matter. We're going to win either way.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Here, this place looks nice and open. Why don't you all rest here for a second?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What about you? You're not going to join us?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: I'm not tired. I'll keep watch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? But...

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Just let him go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay. We'll just share amongst ourselves then. Did you know, Uncle Yip, that the flavor of these cakes changes depending on...

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Halt! Who goes there?

dialogues.speaker: Houzhang
dialogues.text: ...It appears that one's movements were overly conspicuous.

dialogues.speaker: Jiehu
dialogues.text: Enough of your musings. Focus... Focus on the matter at hand.

dialogues.speaker: Jiehu
dialogues.text: Present your exquisite ornaments at once!

dialogues.speaker: Houzhang
dialogues.text: Indeed! Bring them forth readily and without protest.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Ah!? Wh—What do we do...

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: (Hmm. It seems as if these two are acting alone.)

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: (It won't be difficult to subdue them, but they might have something else waiting in store for Dad. The best way to keep him safe is...)

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Leave this to me. I'll handle them.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, take my dad and the goods away from here!

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: No, Gaming! It's too dangerous!

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: This is what I do!

dialogues.speaker: Jiehu
dialogues.text: ...A thorny foe indeed! Let us depart and seek a target softer in blows and disposition!

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Uh-uh, don't think I'm gonna let you off so easily!

dialogues.speaker: Houzhang
dialogues.text: Away! Let us away!

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Gaming!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry! He's a great fighter!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's even seen him take down a dozen or so Treasure Hoarders all by himself!

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: But, Gaming...

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: ...*sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: If he had just stayed by my side and learned the family trade, he wouldn't have to put himself in such dangerous situations.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We just have to trust him. Let's go on ahead. We'd best get away from here, in case there are other bandits in the area waiting in ambush.

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: (All is going to plan...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, we should be good to stop here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zhongli!? Oh no, what is he doing here？

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Good sir, please listen to me. Reel in your line and leave this place as quickly as you can! There are bandits in the area.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Bandits? Acting in broad daylight...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem! *cough* *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Oh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Ah, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It appears many people are catching a chill as of late. If your throat is bothering you, Paimon, perhaps some tea and rest are in order.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Nope! No need. No need. Paimon's fine. She just... had some cake stuck in her throat...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He must have figured it all out by now. Is he just playing dumb on purpose...)

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: If there are indeed bandits in the area, then we should inform the Millelith at once.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The guard that was escorting us is already on their tail.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Oh? Well, if that's the case...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Such matters are best left to those with the necessary expertise, wouldn't you agree?

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: *sigh* I suppose you're right... If ordinary people like us got involved, we would only cause more trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Since we find ourselves otherwise unoccupied in this beautiful area, why don't we find a quiet place to relax while we wait for good news?

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Hmm... That would be lovely.

talks.objective: Find a tea stall to rest at

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, uh, Uncle Yip does have reason to be worried. After all, Gaming, the guard we mentioned, is his son.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Gaming... The name sounds somewhat familiar. Ah yes, that is the name of the Wushou dancer who has been performing around Liyue Harbor recently, is it not?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Have you seen him perform?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed. I cannot help but admire his skill. He truly encapsulates the spirit of the suanni.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Wushou dancing has become more well-known in Liyue Harbor recently. However... Although performers are seeing budding success, they have, no doubt, had to face many hurdles along the way — ones not so easily understood by spectators such as ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: If you ask me, what truly deserves admiration is perseverance in the face of adversity. That is a rare attribute indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I have heard many of my acquaintances praise Gaming for his kind, selfless, and courageous disposition... To have a child so accomplished and upright... You must be a very proud parent indeed, Uncle Yip.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Uncle Yip...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Seems like Zhongli has decided to skip the formalities...)

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Ah, well...

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: He... He's a hard worker, yes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You should be sure to tell him you think that when he gets back!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Your son is young yet. It's normal for someone his age to be a bit... hotheaded.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It's understandable to find talking about such things in person difficult. If there's a particular sentiment you wish to convey, perhaps we could pass it along for you.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: No, no! It wouldn't be right to ask that of you...

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: *sigh* This thing between us has festered for many years now. In truth... there are some things that simply aren't easy for us to talk through.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: I've been in the tea business for most of my life, and I always hoped my child would do the same. Otherwise, how would he support himself?

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Over the past few years, I heard how well he was doing for himself as a guard, how his work was taking him to farther and farther off places... I also heard that he never gave up on Wushou dancing. It made me happy... but I was also worried.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: When you're young, you can handle all that physically taxing work and manual labor. What young person isn't capable of making a living that way? My concern is what happens when you get old.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Every time I get to thinking like that, I cannot help but be reinforced in the belief that I was right... that I was right not to give in.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: I often regret introducing him to Wushou dancing as a kid. If I had known how things would turn out, I would have never taken him to see those performances in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It is only natural for a parent to strive to send their child down the right path. No one would begrudge you that sentiment, Uncle Yip. You need not worry.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: You seem quite young, Mr. Zhongli, yet you speak with such wisdom... Perhaps I have misjudged your age?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Hahaha, your words are too kind. Truth be told, one of my old friends has several grown daughters.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Rather than fretting about their future, however, she prefers to let them find their own way.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Then she is more easygoing than I could ever be. I fear... I lack such an open mind.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Oh, I meant to say earlier, there is no need to be so polite. Feel free to call me by my name, Yip Tak.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: So, do you also think I fret too much, Mr. Zhongli?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: *sigh* That's not exactly what I was hoping to convey. Only a fool would ask a parent not to worry about their child. But think of it this way — raising a child is not unlike flying a kite. Hold the string too tight, and it can no longer soar.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: As my friend once said, if your children are aiming for the stars... clipping their wings will only cause them to come crashing down. You need to let out the line for a kite to soar.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* It seems I was too stuck in my ways.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You need not reproach your heart for caring. You simply need to loosen your hold a little.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed with such a big heart, why not allocate the time you usually spend worrying about Gaming to the pursuit of other things, like going for a stroll, drinking tea, or taking in the scenery? You never know what surprises could be in store — things can change in the blink of an eye.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Haha, the blink of an eye, you say? Do things change so quickly?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Children grow up in quite the same way, do they not? Day after day, year after year, sometimes in the blink of an eye, but always when you least expect it. As a father, I'm sure you know that best.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Haha... Yes, you can say that again... One second, Gaming was a kid, the next thing I knew he was ready to fly the nest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zhongli certainly has a way with words...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Gaming is back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Gaming, we're over here!

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: #Dad, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. Good, you're all here. Oh! And Mr. Zhongli from the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor? You're here too?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Haha, a fated meeting indeed! We were just enjoying some pleasant conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Is everything resolved?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Well, you could say that...

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: What does that mean?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, come with me. I need to talk to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh... Okay...

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: I'll come right out and say it. Those two bandits... You sent them, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? So, that's how we're starting off?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Can't look me in the eye, huh? Guess I'm right, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... But how did you know?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: At first, their mannerisms seemed a bit stilted. But once I got close, it was obvious that they possessed great skills.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: I was right on their tail, and it should have taken only a few steps to catch up to them, yet somehow, I was never able to close that distance...

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: People with that level of skill would have gone about things differently from the start, like sneaking up on us while we were distracted.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Unless, or course, their real motive was to lure me away from the group all along.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you're pretty quick on the uptake!

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: I just have a lot of experience. I've dealt with many a ruthless bandit in my time, but I've never seen ones like them.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: In the end, I told them they would make good guards if they ever wanted to get back on the straight and narrow, and that they could come hang out with me in Liyue Harbor any time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh... You ever consider that you might be a little too good at making friends?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: I'm guessing you guys were trying to help resolve things between my dad and me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: I appreciate it. I really do.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: But this conflict between us has been going on for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Even if those two were real bandits, and I was able to subdue them and show him what I was capable of, it wouldn't change anything...

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: You've seen the way he talks to me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's not like that at all! Your dad really cares about you. You should see the way he talks about you when you're not around!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zhongli was talking things through with him, and he nearly agreed to let it go...

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't believe us?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: He won't let it go. He can say as much as he wants to other people, but he won't talk to me. I'm certain of it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And you? Will you talk to him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You told us you wanted to prove yourself to your dad. Why don't you tell him about all the hard work you've done these past few years?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Will that even do anything? I'm not sure "talking" is enough...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You won't know unless you try! Just like how you won't know if something is delicious unless you taste it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Listen to us. It's time to put these people skills to good use! You can make friends with anyone! So why not your dad?

choices.text: Good luck! We'll be rooting for you.

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Ha...

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: I'll do my best.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: ...You are very knowledgeable, Mr. Zhongli. I'm impressed!

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Despite my being in the tea industry for several decades, it seems I still have much to learn about the art of tea tasting.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: You flatter me. It was nothing but a few humble musings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How much tea have you drank since we've been gone?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's not like it was alcohol...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Haha, Yip Tak and I have found many a common interest. Our friendship, much like a cup of tea, seems to grow stronger the longer it has to steep.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Well said, Mr. Zhongli.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Gaming, Mr. Zhongli is very knowledgeable. You should take the opportunity to learn from people like him when you're in the city.

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Huh? Oh... Of course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahem... Zhongli...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I have very much enjoyed our conversation, Yip Tak, but I, unfortunately, have some unfinished Funeral Parlor business to attend to.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Oh! I hope I didn't keep you.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: My apologies for taking up so much of your time, Mr. Zhongli. No need to stay on my account. When you're less busy, let's find a time to meet. I'll treat you to dim sum.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It would be an honor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll see you off, Zhongli!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You two have a nice chat, alright?

talks.objective: Leave the tea stall and talk to Zhongli
Go to Liyue Harbor to deliver the goods

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: You must be Mr. Yip! Thank you for coming all this way.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: My name is Charlotte, and I am a reporter from Fontaine. You can find me writing for The Steambird. I invited you here not just to purchase your fine tea, but also with the hope that you might be willing to sit down for a short interview. What do you say?

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: An interview? To advertise my teas?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I suppose you could think of it that way. We Fontainians are big tea drinkers too.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: The Fontaine market...

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Then I'll need some time to adequately prepare. Perhaps we could sit down and discuss the questions you intend to ask in advance.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Of course! Of course! Please follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Is this person also involved in your plan?

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: And here I thought I had lots of connections! I suppose I've been humbled. You sure know all kinds of cool and important people.

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Over here... Yoo-hoo! Over here...

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Huh? Aunty Xianyun?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She probably wants to talk about the next phase of the plan! Let's go while your dad is still distracted.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: ...I take it that all is going well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Xianyun. Everything is going according to plan!

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: (I knew it! I knew that was all an act earlier! Aunty Xianyun is really something!)

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: (She was so determined to help me, she didn't even care about making herself and Shenhe appear foolish in front of my family. She truly knows how to look out for others! I still have a lot to learn.)

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: As for the next step...

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Oh, nooooo!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Gaming?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Don't tell me... you're the ones footing the bill for all that tea? I can't let you do that...

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Fret not. Reimbursements will be made.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! Think of it more as an "investment," as Ningguang would say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We pooled together the Mora so that Charlotte could place the order. She's gonna bring it back to The Steambird as a gift, as well as a sample of the regional specialty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fontainians will probably fall in love with your dad's tea as soon as they lay their eyes on Charlotte's article. And once all the money from the new orders begin to roll in, getting our Mora back will be a piece of cake!

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Oh, okay...

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Business-related matters always seem to go over my head, but I refuse to let you all lose Mora on my behalf. I'll pay you back right now...

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: We can talk about such matters at a later date. There are more important matters for you to consider at the moment, are there not?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: ...Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: I've been thinking about it the whole way here.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: I have an idea.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: But I'd hate to cause even more trouble for all of you...

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: That is for us to decide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! We're all friends here. Plus, we wouldn't be here if we didn't want to help, right? Just tell us about this idea of yours!

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Okay! *exhale*... So it's like this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it! Just leave it to us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's split up and make it happen!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We need to do those things we talked about, but we also still have the kite-flying competition.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Since Xiao already tested out those kites for us... Why don't we also go buy one of those mechanical thingamabobs or whatever they're called? We can attach it to our kite!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello again!

dialogues.speaker: Zhenyuan
dialogues.text: Welcome back! I see you've returned from your trip. I really do have to thank you for all your help from before.

dialogues.speaker: Zhenyuan
dialogues.text: Thanks to you, my daughter was able to build a kite with her grandmother that very same day. She even wrote a long letter telling me how much she loved it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you should really be thanking Gaming, not us.

dialogues.speaker: Zhenyuan
dialogues.text: I'll be sure to.

dialogues.speaker: Zhenyuan
dialogues.text: Are you here to buy a kite? Please take your pick!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we already have a kite. We wanted to buy one of those, um... device thingies from Fontaine. Do you sell them separately?

dialogues.speaker: Zhenyuan
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. Here you go. Please take it, free of charge. The directions are in the box. It's not hard to install at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, it doesn't feel right for us to just take it...

dialogues.speaker: Zhenyuan
dialogues.text: Well, nor would it feel right for me to take your Mora. Hehe, good luck in the kite-flying competition. I'll be rooting for you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright then. Thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, it's done!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's get down to business!

talks.objective: Wait for Lantern Rite to begin

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: I think I'll head off now. Is that okay?

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Thank you, little girl. Do you want us to walk you back?

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: No need! No need! Master is waiting for me right over there.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming & Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Dad.\nGaming.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Gaming.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: ...Heh.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: ...I suppose I'll go first this time.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Your performance... I've seen many Wushou dances in my time, but I've got to admit... What you pulled off there was breathtaking.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: ...Wow.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: I never thought I'd live to hear you say that.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: You're... serious about doing this professionally?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Absolutely! I know it'll be difficult, but...

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Then it doesn't matter.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: What I mean to say is, of course it'll be difficult... But if that's your decision, if that's your dream, then it doesn't matter how difficult it is. As long as you put in the work, then any obstacle can be overcome in time.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Really, when I was young, I also... Hehe. Actually, how about we save that story of my past for another time?

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: All I really want to say is, I've changed my mind...

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Much like this kite, you also deserve to soar to new heights.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Dad...

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: ...Son.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Son? ...Haven't heard that in a while...

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: I bet you're wondering what's gotten into me, saying all this...

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: ...Well, uh... Hehehe, a little bit, yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Anyway, I know I've never found the chance to say this before, but... Ahem!

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: To me, Gaming, you've always been a great kid.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Alright. That's everything I've got. Did you have something you wanted to say, or...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seeing the two of them talk things through like this really gives Paimon a sense of accomplishment.

choices.text: Yep, it was all because of you...

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: ...Now go.

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Over there... Your friends are still waiting for you.

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Huh? But, you came all this way...

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: I'll be staying in Liyue Harbor for a bit longer. When you have time, we can grab dim sum together. Your treat, right?

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Dad...! Honestly...

response.speaker: Yip Tak
response.text: Hahaha. Go.

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: ...Okay, then I'm off. See you soon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's quite the smile you've got there, Gaming!

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: R—Really...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's nothing to be embarrassed about!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is there anything else you'd like to do?

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: I'd like to find and thank Aunty Xianyun, as well as everyone else who's helped me out.

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: If everyone has time, maybe we could all get together and...

response.speaker: Gaming
response.text: Go fly a kite.

choices.text: Give yourself a pat on the back, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: Master, did I say something wrong earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: I tried to go along with your questions... But when I saw how you and that man reacted... I started to wonder.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Not at all. Certain unforeseen variables may have presented themselves along the way... but the outcome proved favorable. The plan was a success.

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: Then I helped?

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Your purity of spirit is one of your greatest strengths, Shenhe. You need not change who you are.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Should we sit?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: ...Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: ...Do your teas pair well with milk? What about sugar?

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Uh... Can we skip that question?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Of course. You would much prefer that the teas be made plain, I suppose? Perhaps you could provide some descriptions of their flavor profiles during the interview.

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Ah, no problem.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Noted. Now then, let's discuss tea box design, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Recently, I've learned a lot about traditional Liyue motifs and their deeper meanings. I was thinking, if there was some way to integrate these motifs into the design of the exterior packaging...

dialogues.speaker: Yip Tak
dialogues.text: Now that's an interesting idea. If you ask me, I would probably...
